title: Quickstart insight-tile montage: latency / token-cost / traceflow screenshots
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a compact, production-ready set of onboarding/quickstart UX assets that demonstrate Redwood Console observability: latency distribution tiles, cost-per-token breakdown, and an annotated traceflow view. These assets will be used in the Quickstart docs, in-product first-time experience, and release notes. Deliver a set of responsive screenshots, a montage hero for the docs landing page, and a short animated GIF showing trace zoom+annotation. Prioritize clarity for new users: highlight median vs. p95 latency, identify cost hotspots (model vs. tokens vs. cache hits), and show how traceflow surfaces root causes (kernel stalls, batch wait).
acceptance_criteria: Three final PNG screenshots: latency-tile, cost-token-breakdown, traceflow-annotated (each desktop 1440x900)
One hero montage combining tiles at 1200x600 for docs landing
One lightweight animated GIF (800x450) that demonstrates trace zoom and an inline annotation callout
Assets optimized for dark and light UI themes
Figma file with named frames ready for handoff and export settings documented
Design spec for localization (text safe zones) and platform screenshot sizes (mobile/tablet/desktop)
design_decisions: Use condensed metric tiles for Quickstart to minimize cognitive load: median/p95 latency + simple sparkline
Expose cost per token as stacked bar (model compute | KV cache | I/O) to make trade-offs visible
Traceflow chosen over full flamegraph for onboarding because it tells causal story (request -> model variant -> kernel wait)
Annotations use semi-transparent callout with 24px max copy for readability in docs
Montage layout uses 2-up grid: left latency+cost tiles, right full traceflow to emphasize actionable next steps
